rationale: The pain is real and persistent — Windows developers and power users genuinely suffer from app pollution across AppData and the registry — but the solution is a low-level OS-level filesystem virtualisation tool (kernel-mode drivers, registry hooking, VFS layer), which is categorically unbuildable with Claude prompts, a landing page, and Stripe. Operational autonomy is near-zero because the product itself is native Windows software requiring installation, ongoing maintenance against Windows updates, and deep systems expertise. The buyer segment is nameable (Windows devs/sysadmins) but sprawling and mostly individual — Sandboxie existed and pivoted to free, signalling weak sustained willingness to pay at commercial price points. All four build gates fail badly.
solution_plan: This is not a viable opportunity for a solo non-technical operator running a Claude-based factory. The core requirement is a Windows kernel-mode filesystem and registry virtualisation layer — essentially a lightweight hypervisor or filter driver — which requires C/C++ systems programming, Windows Driver Kit development, code-signing certificates, and continuous compatibility work across Windows versions and updates. There is no Claude-prompt equivalent for this. Even if scoped down to a 'wrapper script that moves AppData to a folder', it would require a native Windows executable, installer, and ongoing QA — none of which this factory can produce or maintain. A non-technical solo operator could not build, sell, or maintain this. The honest recommendation is to drop it entirely.
notes: Fails all four build gates: buildability_with_ai=1 (requires native kernel/driver development, not achievable with Claude + web tooling), operational_autonomy=2 (requires per-update compatibility maintenance and user-side installation support), buyer_clarity=5 (individual developers rarely sustain SaaS payments for dev-environment tooling — see Sandboxie going free), willingness_to_pay=4 (historical precedent of commercial tools collapsing to free/open-source in this niche). This is fundamentally a native Windows systems software product, not a Claude-deliverable micro-service.
